title: Dynamic SLO-triggering service for staged model rollouts
creator: Asha Rao
description: Build a centralized service and evaluation pipeline that watches live SLO signals (latency P95, 5xx rate, token cost per request, throughput) during canary/A-B/shadow experiments and triggers automated rollback or traffic adjustments based on configurable thresholds and adaptive tuning.
goals: Prevent regressions from new model variants by automatically reverting traffic when SLOs degrade
Provide tunable, multi-metric rollback policies with hysteresis to avoid flapping
Expose an operator-friendly UI and API for per-rollout thresholds and auto-tune recommendations
Integrate with existing rollout engine to perform traffic shifts, canary pauses, and forced rollbacks
acceptance_criteria: Service evaluates P95 latency, error rate (5xx+client errors), token-cost-per-request, and throughput over sliding windows and publishes a single health decision per rollout
Automated rollback executes a rollback action in the runtime control plane within 30s of decision and is recorded in rollout audit logs
Default policy contains sane thresholds (e.g., latency +30% over baseline or error-rate +2x) and can be overridden per rollout
Dashboard shows per-rollout metric deltas and reason for rollback with links to traces and PRs
Unit and e2e tests cover detection logic and backoff/hysteresis behavior to prevent repeated flip-flops
technical_design: Architecture: lightweight evaluation service subscribes to rollout events and consumes metric streams from metrics pipeline (Prometheus/Pushgateway) and trace-based sampling signals
Evaluation windowing: dual windows - short (1m) for immediate spikes and medium (5-10m) for sustained regressions; both evaluated before triggering
Metric normalization: convert metrics to z-scores against baseline rollout's distribution and combine via weighted score; weights are configurable per customer and per rollout
Trigger logic: threshold crossing with confirmation count and hysteresis period; require 2 consecutive medium-window violations or 3 short-window spikes before action
Multi-metric policy: support boolean combination (any, all) and weighted scoring; default policy is 'any' with priority order error-rate, latency, token-cost, throughput
Statistical test: use Poisson test for error-rate increases and bootstrap CI for latency shifts to avoid false positives on small sample sizes
Adaptive thresholds: service records signal history and suggests threshold relaxations/tightenings for similar workloads via a recommendations API
Actions: pause canary traffic, route remaining canary traffic to baseline, or perform full rollback; all actions go through gated runtime API with idempotency key
Safety: rate-limit rollbacks to 1 per rollout per 10 minutes; require manual approval for rollbacks that impact >50% of customer traffic
Observability: emit evaluation decisions, raw metric windows, and rationale to telemetry with tags: rollout_id, model_version, region, customer_tier
rollout_scenarios: Canary: 5% traffic to model-v2. If P95 latency increases by >30% for 2 consecutive 5m windows, pause and route 100% to model-v1
A/B: 50/50 split for perf experiment. If error-rate for variant B > 1.5x baseline and absolute error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m, trigger rollback for B
Shadow: send shadow traffic for 100% of requests; no automatic rollback (default), but flag if token-cost per request for shadow > cost threshold and surface as 'cost-warning' in UI
Throughput regression: if throughput drops below 70% of baseline while latency increases, prioritize rollback even if error-rate is unchanged
Cost-driven rollback: if token-cost-per-request increases by >40% and customer_tier != enterprise, recommend rollback and mark as 'high-cost' decision
monitoring_queries: PromQL example for P95 latency delta: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_version))
Token cost per request: sum(rate(tokens_consumed_total[5m])) by (model_version) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (model_version)
Throughput drop detection: compare 5m rate to 30m baseline: rate(requests_total[5m]) / avg_over_time(rate(requests_total[30m])[1h:])
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canaries only): enable auto-eval in internal clusters with default policy, no auto-rollback (alert-only) for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (auto-rollback opt-in): allow orgs to opt-in to auto-rollback with a 24h cooldown and operator email notifications
Phase 3 (auto-rollback default): flip to default-on with conservative thresholds and require manual override to disable; run a second safety audit
Fallback: all rollback actions are reversible and available as 'undo' in console; rollback events create a changelog entry and link to triggering metrics
comments: 2026-02-16 - Asha Rao: Created initial PRD and posted to #rollouts. Requested alignment with SRE on alert thresholds.
2026-02-19 - Miguel Alvarez: Spike complete. Implemented baseline histogram collection and a prototype evaluator that reads from Prometheus. Observed noisy P95 for low-volume canaries.
2026-02-26 - Priya Nambiar (SRE): Recommended requiring minimum sample size before firing latency-based rollbacks; added Poisson error-rate check.
2026-03-02 - Design review by Lina Chen: Suggested adding explicit rationale text for each automated decision in the console and a lightweight explanation for customers.

2026-03-08 - Miguel Alvarez: Implemented confirmation count and hysteresis; started integration tests with rollout engine. Found race condition when rollout finishes during evaluation window; added idempotent action keys.

2026-03-12 - QA (Jamal Thomas): Running e2e smoke tests. Triggered a simulated latency spike and validated rollback action executes and logs reason. Found flaky test when metrics pipeline delay >30s; adding buffering and backfill handling.
